candidates.basis: NL3 requires power-on entry into human driving mode. The source transition tr_0002 is the corresponding authored Power On relation, and the closed model binds it to HumanDriving -> Autonomous with Power_On.
candidates.expected: On the power-on transition, the system enters human driving mode.
candidates.observed: The closed model has a Power_On transition from HumanDriving to Autonomous (transition:line:14); no complete-inventory transition with the required system-to-human-driving endpoint is present.
candidates.reason: The exact Power On consumer is bound to transition:line:14, but its target is Autonomous rather than the required HumanDriving state. The endpoint comparison therefore identifies a wrong target while preserving the transition contract.
candidates.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The source and closed model both contain a Power On transition, but the supplied closed endpoint is Autonomous, so event presence does not rebut the required target mismatch.
candidates.title: Power-on enters the wrong state

candidates.basis: NL4 names system as source and autonomous state as target under front_distance > 10. The source inventory maps this condition to tr_0004 and tr_0007, while the closed inventory binds the corresponding event to transition:line:16 and transition:line:19 with different endpoint pairs.
candidates.expected: When front_distance > 10, the system transitions to autonomous state.
candidates.observed: The closed model's Front_Distance_10_2 transition from AutonomousIdle goes to AutonomousActive (transition:line:16), and its other consumer from HumanDriving goes to Autonomous (transition:line:19); neither is an exact system-to-autonomous-state endpoint as stated by the contract.
candidates.reason: The required event-condition relation is represented by the source as a transition to the autonomous state, but the closed model distributes the corresponding event across concrete transitions with different sources and targets. The exact endpoint requirement is therefore not realized.
candidates.requirement_quote: when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The closed model includes a Front_Distance_10_2 consumer reaching Autonomous from HumanDriving, but that still does not match the contract's exact system-to-autonomous-state endpoint and does not cover the source transition from the autonomous context.
candidates.title: Distance condition reaches the wrong state

candidates.basis: NL4.2 explicitly requires human steering and brake behavior in auto final. The source inventory identifies tr_0005 and tr_0006 from AutonomousActive to HumanDriving, and the closed transition inventory confirms those exact carriers without an Auto Final source.
candidates.expected: Upon the stated human steering command and brake condition in auto final, the system transitions to human driving mode.
candidates.observed: The closed model has Human_Steering_Cmd and Brake_Pressed transitions from AutonomousActive to HumanDriving (transition:line:17 and transition:line:18), but no transition from the required Auto Final context is present in the complete inventory.
candidates.reason: The closed model provides both named response triggers, but they are carried by transitions from AutonomousActive rather than from the supplied auto-final context. The required context-sensitive endpoint relation is therefore not realized.
candidates.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: Both required trigger names and the HumanDriving target are present, but the supplied source/context requirement includes Auto Final and the closed carriers originate in AutonomousActive, so trigger presence alone cannot discharge the scoped endpoint obligation.
candidates.title: Auto-final response is not realized

candidates.basis: The source labels AutonomousFinal as the final state; the closed model binds Power_Off to AutonomousFinal, and deterministic reachability/dead-end facts show the target is reachable and has zero outgoing transitions.
candidates.expected: After power off reaches final state, the system completes there without continued behavior.
candidates.observed: Power_Off reaches AutonomousFinal (transition:line:20), and AutonomousFinal is reachable with no outgoing transition (state:AutonomousFinal:line:12). The supplied facts do not establish a continuation, re-entry, or route out of the target; the no-outgoing fact is consistent with stable completion.
candidates.reason: The termination contract is exact and was audited through the target and its available continuation. The power-off edge reaches the intended final-state identity, and the target has no outgoing transition. Because no supplied fact shows re-entry or continued behavior, there is no supported termination violation to emit.
candidates.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The diagnostic labels the final leaf as a deadlock frontier, but the supplied NL explicitly defines it as a final state, so zero outgoing transitions are compatible with completion and do not independently prove failed termination.
candidates.title: Final state is a stable terminal target
